clue.text: Thankful for sure to be without return of disease

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for sure goes round the turned disease

parts.note: indeed means for sure, certainly

indicators.note: return of means the disease's letters are read backwards

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis, a disease

explanation.surface: Someone grateful that an illness has not come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'to be' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indebted to someone means owing them gratitude, so it is a synonym for thankful.

clue.text: Voiced an unorthodox view of Chopin

indicators.note: an unorthodox view of something sees it rearranged, so the composer's name is reshuffled

explanation.surface: A music critic takes an unconventional angle on the composer Chopin.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonic describes speech sounds, so it means relating to the voice or voiced.

clue.text: Bee leaves plant in ecstasy!

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the letter for the insect drops out of the plant name

parts.note: euphorbia is a plant, the spurge
B is the letter named bee

explanation.surface: A gardener is overjoyed when a bee finally flies off the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bee' is the letter B; 'leaves' removes it from EUPHORBIA, the spurge family of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is a feeling of intense happiness, a synonym for ecstasy.

clue.text: Boy devouring a slice of bread under a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the bread's piece below the second a
devouring means eating up, so the boy's name takes the letter in

parts.note: Bob is a boy's name

indicators.note: a slice of bread here is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A lad eats a piece of bread while sitting under a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: BOB swallows A to give BAOB; then B (the first letter of bread) goes under the second A, giving AB.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is an African tree with a famously thick trunk.

clue.text: Shell injury finally makes one unwilling to fight

parts.note: a conch is a sea shell

indicators.note: finally points to the end letter of the word injury

explanation.surface: A soldier wounded by a shell decides never to fight again.
explanation.walkthrough: CONCHY is British slang for a conscientious objector, someone who refuses military service.
explanation.definitionFit: Conchy is informal for conscientious objector, a person who refuses to take part in war.

clue.text: Conducts church music

parts.note: airs are tunes, pieces of music

explanation.surface: Someone directs the choir's music in church.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to conduct or preside over it.

clue.text: Take odd bits of grub to convicts in prison camps

indicators.note: odd bits are the first and third letters of the word grub

parts.note: lags is slang for convicts, as in old lags

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring food scraps to prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' is British slang for a convict, usually a hardened one ('old lag').
explanation.definitionFit: Gulags were the Soviet forced-labour camps, so the word names prison camps.

clue.text: Spots Hector Sants with leading industrialists

indicators.note: to hector is to bully or push about, so these letters are knocked into a new order
leading picks the front letter of the word industrialists

explanation.surface: A news item about a financial regulator meeting top business figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' looks like a first name, but as a verb it means bully, signalling the anagram of SANTS plus I. Hector Sants was a head of the UK's Financial Services Authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Stains are marks or blemishes, the same as spots on fabric.

clue.text: Perhaps Parisian left Spain with hail and farewell, but unannounced

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective describing a departure, while the answer is a noun phrase for such a departure

parts.note: a Parisian is one example of someone French
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
ave is the Latin greeting used for both hail and farewell

explanation.surface: A Parisian leaves Spain after a greeting and goodbye, yet slips off without telling anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking FRENCH LEAVE means leaving without permission or notice; the definition stands for the phrase as used in 'leave unannounced'.
explanation.definitionFit: French leave is an idiom for slipping away without saying goodbye, an unannounced departure.

clue.text: Beware of sailors in a Liverpool club!

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, schoolboy slang for look out
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A warning about rowdy sailors in a Liverpool nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (pronounced 'kay-vee') was British schoolboy slang for 'look out'. The Cavern Club in Liverpool is where the Beatles played.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavern is the Liverpool music club famous for the early Beatles.

clue.text: Rechabite's disheartened as itinerant male consumes a huge bottle

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart is taken out, leaving only the outer letters of Rechabite
consumes means swallows, so the tramp and the male take in the letter

parts.note: a hobo is an itinerant worker or tramp

explanation.surface: A teetotal Rechabite despairs as a tramp drinks a whole enormous bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Rechabites were a temperance society, so the surface joke is a teetotaller watching a tramp drink heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is a large wine or champagne bottle holding six standard bottles.

clue.text: Regularly take girl out to see a small, poetic 9

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words girl and out

explanation.surface: An invitation to take a girlfriend on a date to see a little cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is CAVERN. GROT is a poetic word for a grotto, a small cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Grot is a literary word for grotto, a small cave, as poets use it.

clue.text: Guerrilla group involved in smuggling

parts.note: the Contras were guerrilla fighters in Nicaragua
a band is a group

explanation.surface: Rebel fighters are caught up in illicit trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband goods are those traded illegally, so the word describes things involved in smuggling.

clue.text: Cognitively challenged tot unexpectedly healed by a combination of vitamins

parts.note: to tot up is to add

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests something turning out differently, so the letters of healed are rearranged

parts.note: E and D are two vitamins named by letters

explanation.surface: A small child is cured surprisingly by a vitamin supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child but is the verb meaning add up; LEHEAD comes from 'healed' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Addleheaded means muddled or stupid, a jokey way of saying cognitively challenged.

clue.text: Repeated prayers force saintliest saint to flee

indicators.note: force means push about, so the letters of saintliest are rearranged once the saint is gone

explanation.surface: A pious instruction to drive out the holiest saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ST ('saint to flee') from the letters of SAINTLIEST; 'force' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Litanies are series of prayers with repeated responses from the congregation.

clue.text: Shares drug and is quite sick

parts.note: E stands for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: sick suggests something upset or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drug and feels rather ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Equities are ordinary shares in a company.

clue.text: Heads and leaders of unruly tribes eliminated old king

parts.note: heads is a naval word for toilet, and can is slang for toilet too

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of unruly, tribes and eliminated

explanation.surface: A ruler wipes out the chiefs of rebellious tribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' (ship's toilets) gives CAN, American slang for a lavatory. Canute was an 11th-century king of England, Denmark and Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute, or Cnut, was an early medieval king of England.

clue.text: Hairy bloodhound's first to locate bone at foot of tree

parts.note: a bloodhound is slang for a detective, a PI or private investigator

indicators.note: first to points to the opening letter of the word locate

parts.note: os is Latin for bone, used in anatomy

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot of a word is its last letter, here of tree

explanation.surface: A tracker dog sniffs out a buried bone beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloodhound' looks like a dog but is slang for a detective, PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilose is a botanical and zoological term for covered with soft hairs.

clue.text: Block off thoroughfare in financial district

parts.note: to wall something is to block it off
a street is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: An order to close a road in a city's banking quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street in Manhattan is New York's financial district and stands for US finance.

clue.text: Ambassador's on at end of conference

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word conference

explanation.surface: A diplomat is present at the close of a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the 'on' side of the field is also called the leg side, so on gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy or ambassador, especially one representing the Pope.

clue.text: Merchant causing some scared artisans to recoil

indicators.note: to recoil is to spring back, so the letters run backwards
some means only part of the phrase scared artisans is used

explanation.surface: A dealer frightens a few craftsmen into shrinking away.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'scaRED ARTisans' is REDART; 'to recoil' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is someone who buys and sells goods, a merchant.

clue.text: The individual is part of the community

indicators.note: is part of says the letters sit inside the word community

explanation.surface: A social observation that each person belongs to the wider society.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single individual thing or person regarded as one of a whole.

clue.text: In France you never should go wild about German writer

parts.note: tu is French for you

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled word goes round the letter for German
going wild means running out of control, so the letters of never are scrambled

explanation.surface: Advice that in France you should never lose your head about a German.
explanation.walkthrough: RENEV, from 'never' going wild, goes around G. Ivan Turgenev was a Russian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a 19th-century Russian novelist and playwright, so a writer.

clue.text: Hour at which working writer may be seen

indicators.note: working means being shaped or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The time of day when an author can be found at their desk.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is someone who writes books, so a writer.

clue.text: Woman and husband entering compound

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the letter for husband sits within the compound

parts.note: an ester is a chemical compound

explanation.surface: A wife and husband move into a walled residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a woman's name, also a biblical queen.

clue.text: Trying to divorce partner

parts.note: to sever is to cut off or divorce
in bridge East partners West, so E is a partner

explanation.surface: It is hard to separate from a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, players sit as North, South, East and West, with opposite players partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh or demanding, as in a trying ordeal.
